summary: Bound seat identity and pin reference lengths — no maxLength exists anywhere in the catalog contract
description:
Surfaced as an incidental finding by TKT-112's ai-review pass 3 (deliberately not fixed there — it is a public-contract change, outside that ticket's scope).

**The gap.** Nothing bounds the length of a seat identity or a pin reference:

- `seat_map_pins.seat_identity` and `seat_map_pins.pinned_by` are unbounded `text` (`services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0011_seat_map_edit_pinning.sql:58,62`). Same for the seat/row/section labels the identity is composed from (`0009_seat_maps.sql`).
- The **seat-map authoring fields carry no `maxLength`**: `SeatMapCreate.name`, `SeatMapSectionCreate.name`, `SeatMapRowCreate.label` and `SeatMapSeatCreate.label` each have `minLength: 1` and a `^[^/]+$` pattern and no upper bound (`services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:2481,2526,2537,2547`).
- The only bound in play is `http.MaxBytesReader(..., 1<<20)` on whole request bodies (`services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:228,522`), so a single seat identity can approach 1 MiB on its own.

**A house convention now exists, and it narrows this ticket sharply.** When this was filed there was
no bounded string anywhere in the catalog contract. There are now **19 `maxLength` constraints** in
`openapi.yaml` (added by TKT-190 auth, TKT-235 channels, and the fee-rule work), and
`migrations/0018_channels.sql:38-42` states the rule in its own comment while bounding
`display_name` to 1..200:

> Bounded like every other display string in this schema; 1..200 matches `payees.display_name`
> (0017), the nearest sibling. An unbounded text column on an operator-writable table is a storage
> and index problem waiting (**TKT-143 tracks the class**).

So the de-facto numbers are **1..100 for codes and 1..200 for display strings**, and this ticket is
now largely "confirm those apply to seat-map labels and pin references", not "invent limits".

**Why it matters.** Any consumer that has to size a response has no contract to size it against. TKT-112's `reconcile-pins` hit this directly: it caps a pin page at 4 MiB and, because no producer bound exists, has to treat an overflow as retryable and halve the page rather than rely on a computed worst case. That works, but the cap is a guess. The same guess will have to be re-made by every future reader of these fields.

**Decide, then implement.** `maxLength` in the OpenAPI schema plus matching `CHECK` constraints,
following 0018's shape. A length limit on an already-populated authoring field is a behaviour change
for existing seat maps, so it needs a migration story — that is the remaining design work.

**Not urgent.** No correctness or security consequence today: TKT-112 fails safe (it never deletes a pin it could not fully read) and can always make progress by shrinking. This is about replacing a guessed constant with a contract.

---

**Updated by TKT-112's ai-review pass 4 — this ticket now owns a live limitation, not just a tidiness gap.**

Pass 4 showed the unbounded fields are worse than "no contract to size against": they make a row **unreadable**, and an unreadable row stops `reconcile-pins` at that cursor. Catalog serializes with `json.NewEncoder`, which HTML-escapes `<`, `>`, `&` into six-byte sequences (control characters expand identically), so a ~1 MiB field of those lists as ~6 MiB and exceeds the client's 4 MiB cap even at one row per page. The keyset cursor cannot advance past a row that was never read, so every later pin becomes unreclaimable until the offending pin is deleted by hand.

Accepted as a limitation in TKT-112 at the review churn cap, documented in `docs/development.md` §Seat-pin reconciliation (`:139-146`) and on `ErrSeatPinPageTooLarge` (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/catalog.go:175-201`). Not blocking there because nothing the system writes can trigger it (`pinned_by` is `"hold:" + uuid`; identities are composed server-side from labels), the failure is loud and names the cursor, and no pin is wrongly deleted.

**So this ticket's scope grew by one item:** after the length bound exists, either derive the reconciliation cap from it and drop the shrink-on-overflow retry, or keep the retry as belt-and-suspenders and say which. Note that disabling HTML escaping on the pin-list response would *narrow* the expansion but not close it — control characters expand the same way — so it is not a substitute for the bound.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=note -->
Created by TKT-112's autonomous run from ai-review pass 3's incidental finding. Triaged as incidental rather than blocking: real, but fixing it inside TKT-112 would have meant changing the public OpenAPI contract and the seat-map authoring validation, which the ticket and plan did not anticipate.

Minimal mémo for whoever picks this up:
- **Source ticket:** TKT-112 (PR #128), ai-review pass 3, finding `[medium]`.
- **Code pointers:** `services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0011_seat_map_edit_pinning.sql:58,62` · `0009_seat_maps.sql` (labels) · `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` (no maxLength at all) · `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:119,273` (the 1 MiB request bounds) · `services/inventory/internal/consumer/catalog.go` (`maxSeatPinPageBytes`, the guessed constant this would replace).
- **Suspected governing ADRs:** ADR-009 (contract-first — the spec is where a length bound belongs), ADR-022/ADR-008 (a CHECK constraint on populated columns needs a migration story), ADR-019 (if any read is re-shaped).
- **It is a decision, not just an edit** — what the limits are, and whether existing over-long data is rejected, truncated, or grandfathered. So it needs the plan gate.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=note -->
Second finding from the same root cause, this time from TKT-112's ai-review **pass 4**: the missing length bound does not just leave consumers guessing, it lets one row wedge the reconciliation drain. Description updated. The reviewer's recommendation was to enforce producer-side maximum ENCODED sizes and derive the consumer cap from them — note *encoded*, since JSON escaping is where the 6x expansion happens.

A test worth writing here that TKT-112 could not: drive the real catalog JSON encoder and the real `CatalogResolver` over HTTP with escaping-heavy near-limit data, and prove a one-row page stays readable and later rows still drain. TKT-112's shrink test injects the sentinel by page size and never crosses the real encoder boundary, so it cannot see this class.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### STILL VALID — one claim in the description is now FALSE and must be corrected before planning

Backlog review 2026-08-26 at HEAD `1aaee7cd`.

**The load-bearing gap is intact.** `seat_map_pins.seat_identity` and `pinned_by` are still unbounded `text` (`services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0011_seat_map_edit_pinning.sql:58,62`), and the seat-map authoring fields still carry `minLength: 1` and a pattern but **no `maxLength`** (`openapi.yaml:2481, 2526, 2537, 2547`).

**DRIFTED CLAIM — correct it.** The description says openapi.yaml contains *"**zero** `maxLength` constraints — not on seat-map authoring fields, not anywhere"*. False at HEAD: there are **19**, added by later tickets (`openapi.yaml:990, 1132, 1872, 1876, 2141, 2242-2243, 2269, 2358, …`). Still true *for the seat-map and pin fields*, which is the part that matters — but as written the sentence would mislead a planner into thinking no convention exists.

**And a convention does now exist, which narrows the decision sharply.** `migrations/0018_channels.sql:41` bounds channel `display_name` to 1..200 and says in its own comment: *"an unbounded text column on an operator-writable table is a storage and index problem waiting (TKT-143 tracks the class)"*. The de-facto house numbers are 1..100 for codes and 1..200 for display strings. When filed this was an open "what should the limits be"; today it is largely "confirm the house numbers apply here".

**Line drift (minor):** the body-size bound is at `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:228` and `:522`, not `:119,273`. Value and symbol unchanged.

**The pass-4 limitation is live and correctly described:** `services/inventory/internal/consumer/catalog.go:175-201` (`maxSeatPinPageBytes = 4<<20`, `ErrSeatPinPageTooLarge`, the 6× HTML-escape expansion argument, "tracked by TKT-143"), and `docs/development.md:139-146`.

**Verdict: near-Ready.** Needs the false sentence struck and the owner confirming the numbers. Then the migration story for already-populated columns is the only real design work.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Description corrected — the "zero maxLength" claim was false, and a precedent has appeared

Re-verified at HEAD `1aaee7cd` before editing.

**Struck:** *"`services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` contains **zero** `maxLength` constraints — not on
seat-map authoring fields, not anywhere."* There are **19** at HEAD. Left as written, that sentence
would have sent a planner looking for a convention that exists, concluding none does, and inventing
numbers.

**Replaced with** the precise, still-true version — the four named seat-map authoring fields carry no
`maxLength` — plus the convention the ticket predates: `migrations/0018_channels.sql:38-42` bounds
`display_name` 1..200, cites `payees.display_name` as its sibling, and **names TKT-143 as the tracker
for the class**. De-facto house numbers: 1..100 codes, 1..200 display strings.

**Line drift fixed:** `MaxBytesReader` is at `server.go:228` and `:522`, not `:119,273`.

**Effect on readiness:** this moves from "decide what the limits should be" to "confirm the house
numbers apply here". The remaining design work is the migration story for already-populated columns.
Near-Ready; one owner confirmation in the decision brief.
